notes: A music video no longer goes quiet about a minute in. The sharp sizes carry no sound of their own, so the app pairs them with the same video’s audio — and for a music upload the site serves that audio cut off at its first megabyte, which is about fifty-seven seconds of a three-minute film. The sharp picture now takes its sound from the same video’s single-file copy, which is not cut. The picture stays sharp and the sound runs to the last frame.

A video that really is shorter than the song is never shown as the video any more. The moment a film says how long it actually is, one under half the song is stepped past for the next result; when nothing better is left, the cover is the picture and the song plays on — instead of a minute of somebody’s cut and then silence.

If a soundtrack does run out before the picture, the film keeps playing: the sound hands on to the single-file copy, or to the song under the picture, rather than the tab sitting in silence on a moving picture.
The line under the picture says which of those is happening, so the size, the sound and the song underneath are never a guess.
